facts.text: Global average daily screen time is about 6h40m (DataReportal); under ~3h counts as light use.
Mobile screen time above ~5h/day correlates with reported sleep and focus problems in population studies.
The average person checks their phone ~58 times a day; heavy users exceed 100.
Screen use in the hour before bed measurably delays sleep onset; heavy late-night use (>60min) is a strong predictor of next-day fatigue.
Typical users spend under ~15% of daily screen time after 11pm.
Social media averages ~2.5h/day globally; anything under 30min/day is far below the norm.
Short, frequent social sessions (checking loops) are the dominant pattern — sessions under 2 minutes drive most pickups.
Sessions longer than 20 minutes are where most 'lost time' concentrates; cutting even one per day is a meaningful win.
Behavior-change research favors small caps: reducing the worst app's time by ~25% for a week outperforms quit attempts.
A protected morning window (no feeds before) is among the highest-leverage digital habits studied.
